requirements.requirement: The account datauser exists and has usable storage under /srv/data.
requirements.summary: datauser was created with /srv/data as its home; the directory is owned by datauser with mode 0700, and the user successfully created a marker file there. These facts remained present after restart.

requirements.requirement: Storage under /srv/data is limited to 100 MB by filesystem enforcement.
requirements.summary: XFS project-quota accounting and enforcement were enabled, /srv/data was assigned a 100 MiB hard limit, and direct writes by datauser stopped at the quota boundary with ENOSPC. The limit and enforcement behavior were demonstrated both before and after restart.

overall_summary: The task is satisfied. A filesystem-enforced XFS project quota limits datauser's private /srv/data directory to 100 MiB, and direct boundary tests confirm enforcement. The mandatory node-restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered SSH, data, mount options, and quota behavior are all captured.
limitations: Package-manager consistency could not be assessed because both lifecycle package-health checks timed out.
The requested “100 MB” was implemented and tested as 100 MiB (100×1,048,576 bytes), which is consistent with the tooling's 100m unit but slightly larger than decimal 100 MB.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear roles: enabling persistent XFS project quotas, creating the account and directory, configuring the limit, bounded write testing, activating the mount option, and completing the mandatory restart protocol. Test payloads were removed and no failed services or new listeners remained. The only hygiene defect is four small executor-created temporary artifacts left in /tmp: quota-enable-reboot.log from cmd-4df9adec62b94192, quota-test.err from cmd-175708d817ce47d1, mandatory-reboot.log from cmd-bc758457fb304694, and post-restart-quota.err from cmd-ed7b55af921342e0. They remained after completion. No unnecessary state-changing experiment was identified.
